This story feels like déjà vu because it was my life. My brothers and I were raised by our aunt, and what we endured still doesn’t sound real when I say it out loud.
Beatings. Deadbolts locked from the inside. Windows and refrigerators sealed shut. No privacy. Constant humiliation. Emotional torture disguised as “care.” We were worked like adults, starved like prisoners—dumpster diving, junking and stealing just to eat. Forced to walk the streets collecting Newport cigarette packs so she could redeem the barcodes.  We had to find 20 each.  That kind of wickedness.
Neighbors knew. They snuck us food when they could. My brother was locked in the basement and I saved my lunch from school and snuck it to him through the laundry chute.. They rode him around in the trunk of a car. There was even a failed plot to get us killed for insurance money.
People knew. That’s why other parents wouldn’t let their kids stay too long.
We survived. Barely. And I’m writing a book because stories like this don’t get told enough, and silence only protects the monsters.
